goal: Bind every shipped client and server gateway to one bounded opaque exact-match protocol version, reject every non-match before operational side effects, explain the typed cause per server, and permanently forbid cross-version compatibility or fallback.
approach: Use a protocol manifest as the only version owner, gate authenticated/no-auth REST and version-bound WebSocket tickets at the server boundary, propagate one generated client token through every host, retain mismatch as a generation-fenced per-server fleet outcome, and enforce flag-day-only evolution with a closed surface inventory and mutation-tested conformance gates.

in_scope: Protocol manifest, generated projections, OpenAPI binding, SDKs, simulator, fakes, and fixtures
Server REST authentication/version precedence and version-bound WebSocket admission
Web, Workspace, Windows, and shared UI typed mismatch propagation and server-list presentation
Supersession of the two-axis capability-negotiation policy and persistent exact-match/no-fallback governance
out_of_scope: Cross-version conversion, compatibility ranges, feature negotiation, downgrade, fallback, or mixed-version rollout
User-configurable expected versions or servers.json version overrides
Versioning internal daemon IPC, agent-specific protocols, or orchestrator protocols

components.name: Protocol version SSOT
components.responsibility: Own the bounded opaque token, exact-equality semantics, typed mismatch schema, and generated language projections.

repo_grounding.rationale: The current protocol version is advertised from code and fixtures without a single machine-readable owner.

components.name: Server gateway version admission
components.responsibility: Own authentication precedence, common REST version admission, typed 426 failures, and version-bound WebSocket tickets.

repo_grounding.rationale: The gateway advertises a version but does not currently enforce it before REST or WS work.

components.name: Protocol policy and carrier conformance
components.responsibility: Own all-host version continuity, the permanent no-compatibility policy, closed surface inventory, and deterministic gates.

repo_grounding.rationale: A shared semantic owner is required because carrier continuity and fallback decisions otherwise remain distributed across hosts.

components.name: Shared fleet compatibility outcome
components.responsibility: Own the closed per-server outcome partition, observation generation fencing, terminal mismatch state, and healthy-peer preservation.

repo_grounding.rationale: Current boolean/string health outcomes erase mismatch meaning and host retry terminality.

components.name: Server-list mismatch presentation
components.responsibility: Render current server labels and typed client/server version evidence without owning transport decisions.

repo_grounding.rationale: Presentation ownership must remain separate from carrier/fleet outcome creation.

components.name: Web, Workspace, and Windows host adapters
components.responsibility: Consume generated versions, preserve credentials and routing boundaries, decode typed mismatch, and suppress operations after mismatch.

repo_grounding.rationale: Delivery transports differ, but compatibility meaning and terminality must not.

components.name: SDK, simulator, and fake conformance
components.responsibility: Keep generated consumers and deterministic test doubles on the same exact-match contract as the production gateway.

repo_grounding.rationale: A production-only gate would allow fakes and SDKs to validate behavior the real system rejects.

requirements.statement: The protocol shall use one 1-64 byte [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ opaque token and compatibility shall mean exact byte equality only.
requirements.rationale: Closes token grammar, malformed classification, and bounded comparison.

requirements.statement: Authenticated protected requests and explicitly unauthenticated routes shall pass one version gate before operational handlers.
Invalid protected credentials shall retain 401/403 without version disclosure; otherwise missing, duplicate, malformed, or unequal versions shall return typed 426 with zero operational effects.
WebSocket admission shall consume a single-use version-bound ticket before hello or application frames.
While a server is incompatible_protocol, every host shall suppress operational REST, WS open, reconnect, degradation, and fallback until a later exact-match probe.
Concurrent matching, mismatching, and unavailable servers shall retain independent latest-generation outcomes and matching peers shall remain operable.
A mismatch server row shall show current label, typed cause, client version, and server version or explicit missing/invalid markers.
Every public protocol change shall bump the token and atomically update server, shipped hosts, SDKs, simulator/fakes, fixtures, and verification.
The repository shall never introduce ranges, SemVer compatibility, capability degradation, legacy or dual decoders, downgrade, retry fallback, or another cross-version success path.
The exact-match ADR shall supersede the two-axis capability-negotiation policy while retaining schema and cross-language generation authorities.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Authentication precedes version disclosure on protected routes; versions are public diagnostics and never credentials or URL query secrets.
Validation performs one constant-bounded comparison per admission/bootstrap and no per-message negotiation.
non_functional_requirements.measurement: At most 64 compared bytes and one compatibility decision per request admission.

non_functional_requirements.criteria: Existing per-server timeout, cancellation, generation, partial-failure, credential confinement, and redirect rejection remain unchanged.
A closed public-surface inventory fails CI when incomplete or when a surface bypasses exact-equality or typed outcome chokepoints.
Both old/new cross-pair directions fail identically and no rollout or rollback compatibility mode exists.

acceptance.given: Representative authenticated read/write routes and an effect counter
acceptance.when: Exact, missing, duplicate, malformed, older, and newer tokens are sent
acceptance.then: Only exact match executes the handler; every other authenticated/no-auth case is typed 426 with zero effects.
The existing auth failure is returned without version evidence.

acceptance.given: One matching and one mismatching configured server
acceptance.when: Web, Workspace, and Windows refresh their fleets
acceptance.then: The matching server remains operable and the mismatching row shows typed cause and version evidence with zero operational/reconnect attempts.

acceptance.when: A range, dual decoder, capability degradation, renamed fallback retry, or unregistered surface is introduced

decision_inputs.subject: Cross-language generated projections
decision_inputs.candidate: generated C#/Swift/Kotlin/TS and stdlib-only Go projection without legacy authority

adrs.title: Require exact-match client-server protocol versions and forbid compatibility fallback

status_provenance.rationale: The user explicitly mandated a permanent development contract forbidding cross-version compatibility and fallback.

adrs.context: The accepted two-axis policy permits version-skew capability degradation and missing-version lowest-capability behavior, which conflicts with the explicit permanent no-compatibility/no-fallback requirement.
adrs.decision: Use one bounded opaque build-time token, exact equality only, authenticated/no-auth pre-side-effect REST and version-bound WS admission, typed per-server mismatch evidence, and flag-day-only evolution; supersede the two-axis policy in full.
consequences: Positive: deterministic compatibility and actionable per-server failures across every host.
Negative: mixed-version rollout and rollback availability are intentionally unavailable.
Neutral: schema ownership and cross-language generated SDK decisions remain in force.

alternatives.why_not: It permits cross-version success and violates the permanent ban.
It creates a compatibility policy instead of opaque exact equality.
It cannot prevent forgotten clients or preflight-to-use side effects.

decision_dispositions.rationale: Fixed by the bounded token and server admission contracts.
Fixed by the superseding ADR, evolution contract, and closed conformance gate.
Fixed as a generation-fenced typed server outcome and presenter input.
Retains protocol/ and OpenAPI ownership under the version contract.
All host adapters consume the same continuity and fleet contracts.
Generalized to all public protocol changes with no compatibility exception.
Its version-skew degradation and missing-version lowest-capability branches are superseded by the new ADR.
T0-T3 verification and the external-dependency fake/fidelity/contract triple are fixed by each contract.
Generated non-Go projections and stdlib-only Go remain constraints; incremental TS migration cannot retain an old version authority or fallback.

implementation_contracts.subject: Bounded protocol token ownership and flag-day-only evolution
related_units: Define protocol token and flag-day evolution

decision_rules.condition: Both bounded generated tokens are present and byte-equal.
decision_rules.outcome: The artifacts are compatible for this source revision.
decision_rules.rationale: Exact equality is the only compatibility predicate.

decision_rules.condition: Tokens are unequal or a projection is absent or malformed.
decision_rules.outcome: Build/conformance fails or runtime admission reports mismatch; no compatibility path is selected.
decision_rules.rationale: Invalid projections and non-match never receive a default.

observable_effects.description: All shipped artifacts from one revision expose one bounded token; drift and every cross-version pairing fail without fallback.

operational_inputs.stability_basis: One checked-out source revision and projection drift gate
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: Any manifest change invalidates every projection and requires atomic regeneration.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Build and conformance fail; no guessed version.

semantic_profiles.surface: All public REST/WS schemas, required fields, routes, and behavioral contracts
semantic_profiles.migration_strategy: Bump one opaque token and update every typed consumer, fixture, fake, simulator, and gate in one change.
semantic_profiles.rollback: Revert the entire source revision and artifacts; never add a compatibility bridge.

semantic_profiles.workload_axis: Protocol token length and request admissions
semantic_profiles.bound: At most 64 bytes and one exact comparison per admission/bootstrap
semantic_profiles.resource_cap: No per-message capability negotiation state or round trip

invariants: The manifest is the only version authority.
Every public protocol change is a breaking flag-day change with no compatibility or fallback.

verification.method: Manifest grammar, projection equality, old/new cross-pair, and atomic-bump contract tests.
verification.criterion: Every artifact has the exact manifest token; 1/64-byte values pass, 0/65/invalid values fail, and no cross-pair succeeds.

witnesses.precondition: All artifacts are generated from one valid manifest revision.
expected_observables: All tokens are identical and bounded; same-revision pairing is admitted.
forbidden_outcomes: A projection supplies an independent default or range.

witnesses.precondition: One projection is stale, token is invalid, or old/new artifacts are paired.
witnesses.stimulus: Run build/conformance and runtime cross-pair fixtures.
expected_observables: The gate or admission fails and no degradation, downgrade, or fallback occurs.
forbidden_outcomes: Range comparison, lowest-capability behavior, or cross-version success.

implementation_contracts.subject: Authenticated REST and version-bound WebSocket admission before side effects
related_units: Gate server REST and WebSocket admission

decision_rules.condition: A protected route has missing or invalid credentials.
decision_rules.outcome: Return existing 401/403 without version evidence and without handler effects.

decision_rules.condition: Authentication succeeds or route is no-auth, and the one bounded request token exactly equals the server token.
decision_rules.outcome: Dispatch the handler once and allow a version-bound ticket to be minted.
decision_rules.rationale: Exact match is the only admitted state.

decision_rules.condition: Authentication succeeds or route is no-auth, and the request token is missing, duplicate, malformed, or unequal.
decision_rules.outcome: Return typed 426 evidence and execute no handler or WS application frame.
decision_rules.rationale: Unknown or nonmatching client compatibility fails closed.

decision_rules.condition: The server build token is unavailable or invalid.
decision_rules.outcome: Fail build/start; do not advertise or assume compatibility.
decision_rules.rationale: An invalid server authority cannot produce a trustworthy runtime response.

observable_effects.description: Auth failures preserve auth semantics; exact match alone reaches handlers and version-bound WS; every version error is typed and side-effect-free.

operational_inputs.required_until: Admission and optional ticket mint complete
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: Missing, duplicate, malformed, or unequal input selects typed 426 after auth.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Typed 426 with missing/invalid client marker after auth.
Server fails closed and does not advertise compatibility.

operational_inputs.source: Existing TokenAuth result or explicit no-auth route declaration
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: Failed auth terminates before version evaluation.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Existing auth failure without version disclosure.

semantic_profiles.coverage_basis: Auth result and bounded version evidence partition every request before dispatch.
semantic_profiles.exclusivity_basis: Auth failure terminates first; otherwise exactly one of equal, invalid/nonmatch, or invalid server authority applies.
semantic_profiles.precedence: Protected auth failure; server validity; request token syntax; exact equality; dispatch.
semantic_profiles.default_policy: Any unclassified or inconclusive condition fails closed.

invariants: No nonmatching request executes an operational handler.
WS frames require a single-use ticket bound to the admitted version.

failure_semantics.outcome: Typed 426 with available client/server evidence and zero effects.

verification.method: Gateway scenario, compound auth/version table, handler effect counter, and ticket lifecycle tests.
verification.criterion: Only exact authenticated/no-auth requests execute; auth failures do not disclose versions; every ticket failure precedes frames.

witnesses.precondition: Valid auth/no-auth declaration and equal bounded tokens.
witnesses.stimulus: Call representative read/write routes, mint a ticket, and open WS once.
expected_observables: Handlers execute once and WS emits frames only after ticket consume.
forbidden_outcomes: Extra negotiation or multiple ticket use.

witnesses.precondition: Invalid bearer plus mismatch, or authenticated missing/duplicate/malformed/unequal version, or stale/replayed ticket.
witnesses.stimulus: Exercise the same REST and WS entry points.
expected_observables: Auth wins when invalid; otherwise typed 426; handler/frame counters remain zero.
forbidden_outcomes: Version disclosure before auth, operational side effect, or legacy WS continuation.

implementation_contracts.subject: All-host version continuity and terminal mismatch behavior
related_units: Propagate exact version through every client host

decision_rules.condition: A host sends its immutable generated token and receives an exact-match response for the current server generation.
decision_rules.outcome: Operational REST and WS are enabled for that server.
decision_rules.rationale: The current exact-match observation authorizes operations.

decision_rules.condition: A host receives authoritative typed mismatch for a server and observation generation.
decision_rules.outcome: Set incompatible_protocol and perform zero operational, reconnect, degradation, or fallback attempts until a later exact-match probe.
decision_rules.rationale: Mismatch is terminal for the observation, not transient transport failure.

observable_effects.description: Web, Workspace, and Windows attach the same token at every hop, classify the same evidence identically, and stop work after mismatch without exposing credentials.

operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Client does not connect with a guessed/configured version.

operational_inputs.source: ServerId and observation-generation keyed bootstrap result
operational_inputs.acquired_at: Fleet refresh or existing compatibility probe cadence
operational_inputs.required_until: Superseding generation, server removal, or host close
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: A newer generation replaces the state; stale completion is discarded.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: That server is unavailable, never inferred compatible or mismatched.

invariants: Every host uses one immutable generated token across all hops.
Mismatch is terminal for the server and observation generation.
Network retry behavior remains distinct and no mismatch retry/fallback occurs.

failure_semantics.outcome: Typed terminal incompatible_protocol with zero operations until later exact match.
Existing bounded network retry policy applies without changing protocol classification.

verification.method: One recorded scenario matrix drives Web request capture, Electron injected fetch/IPC, and Windows HttpMessageHandler/fake-clock tests.
verification.criterion: Every hop sends one token; mismatch yields the same typed state and zero operation/reconnect count on all three hosts.

witnesses.precondition: Current server generation returns exact match.
witnesses.stimulus: Run bootstrap, operational REST, ticket mint, and WS through each host.
expected_observables: Every host preserves token continuity and enables the same server operations.
forbidden_outcomes: Host-specific compatibility meaning or credential exposure.

witnesses.precondition: A hop drops/replaces the token or a current generation returns typed mismatch while stale/network results also complete.
witnesses.stimulus: Advance retry clocks and attempt operational REST/WS.
expected_observables: Mismatch remains current, operation and reconnect counts stay zero, and stale completion cannot overwrite it.
forbidden_outcomes: Capability degradation, renamed fallback retry, or stale compatible overwrite.

implementation_contracts.subject: Generation-fenced per-server outcome and mismatch presentation
related_units: Project fleet mismatch into server lists

decision_rules.condition: Latest generation has authoritative exact-match evidence.
Latest generation has authoritative typed mismatch evidence.
decision_rules.outcome: Server is incompatible_protocol and row shows label, cause, and version evidence/markers.
decision_rules.rationale: Typed mismatch must remain distinct from transport unavailability.

decision_rules.condition: Latest generation has auth/network/timeout failure without authoritative mismatch.
decision_rules.outcome: Only that server is unavailable with its own typed transport reason.
decision_rules.rationale: Unavailable evidence cannot infer protocol mismatch.

decision_rules.condition: The same current generation contains contradictory authoritative exact-match and mismatch evidence.
decision_rules.outcome: Fail closed for that server, expose a typed evidence conflict, and preserve unrelated peers.
decision_rules.rationale: Conflicting authority cannot be resolved by optimistic precedence.

decision_rules.condition: Evidence generation is stale, server was removed, or label/evidence identity cannot be joined.
decision_rules.outcome: Discard stale evidence and never erase unrelated current outcomes.

observable_effects.description: Each current server row shows its current label and exclusive typed state; mismatch shows client/server values or missing/invalid markers while healthy peers remain operable.

operational_inputs.required_until: Rename, removal, superseding generation, or host close
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: Rename replaces label; removal expires the row and evidence.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: No stale label is displayed for a removed server.

operational_inputs.source: ServerId and observation-generation keyed typed bootstrap evidence
operational_inputs.required_until: Next generation, server removal, or host close
operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: New generation replaces evidence; stale completion is discarded.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Preserve available values and explicit missing/invalid markers; otherwise typed unavailable, never generic mismatch.

semantic_profiles.coverage_basis: Latest per-server evidence is exact-match, authoritative mismatch, other typed failure, conflicting, or stale/inconclusive.
semantic_profiles.exclusivity_basis: One serverId and current generation selects exactly one closed outcome; contradictory authority selects conflicting.
semantic_profiles.precedence: Discard stale; detect conflicting authority; authoritative exact/mismatch; typed auth/network/timeout; otherwise inconclusive.
semantic_profiles.default_policy: Never infer compatibility or mismatch from missing evidence.

semantic_profiles.partial_data_behavior: Update only completed server outcomes, retain current healthy peers, and fence stale generations.

invariants: Each configured server has one exclusive latest-generation outcome.
Mismatch evidence is never flattened to unavailable.
Presentation joins current label and current evidence by serverId only.

failure_semantics.outcome: Display incompatible_protocol and evidence while preserving peers.
Display that typed failure without changing other server outcomes.

verification.method: Pure reducer/presenter tests plus Web smoke and Windows UIA backstop with rename, removal, stale generation, malformed evidence, and mixed fleet.
verification.criterion: Current label and evidence remain aligned; mismatch is explicit; healthy peer remains operable.

witnesses.precondition: Two current servers: one exact match and one typed mismatch.
witnesses.stimulus: Render the server list and operate the matching server.
expected_observables: The matching peer remains operable and the mismatching row shows label, cause, and both versions.
forbidden_outcomes: Fleet-wide failure or generic unavailable mismatch.

witnesses.precondition: A rename/removal races with stale, contradictory, and malformed/missing evidence while another server is healthy.
witnesses.stimulus: Complete observations out of order and render.
expected_observables: Only current serverId/generation evidence appears, with explicit markers or evidence conflict; healthy peer remains.
forbidden_outcomes: Old label/new evidence join, blank reason, stale row, or peer erasure.

implementation_contracts.subject: Closed protocol surface inventory and mutation-tested no-fallback enforcement

decision_rules.condition: Every declared route, host, decoder, retry site, SDK, fake, simulator, and fixture is registered and passes exact-match scenarios.
decision_rules.rationale: A closed inventory makes the global claim enumerable.

decision_rules.condition: A registered target cannot execute or return authoritative conformance evidence.
decision_rules.outcome: Conformance fails and names the unavailable target.
decision_rules.rationale: Unavailable evidence cannot establish global compliance.

decision_rules.condition: A public surface is unregistered, skipped, or cannot produce evidence.
decision_rules.outcome: Conformance fails and names the missing surface.
decision_rules.rationale: Inconclusive coverage cannot count as success.

decision_rules.condition: A mutation introduces range comparison, dual decode, capability degradation, renamed fallback retry, or an alternate decision chokepoint.
decision_rules.outcome: Dependency/scenario/mutation gate fails even if advisory word scanning misses the name.
decision_rules.rationale: Structural ownership and behavior, not vocabulary, discriminate fallback.

observable_effects.description: Any compatibility branch, bypass, projection drift, fake divergence, or inventory gap becomes a deterministic named CI failure before merge.

operational_inputs.invalidation_behavior: Surface or target change requires explicit inventory and scenario update.
operational_inputs.unavailable_outcome: Verification is inconclusive and fails closed.

semantic_profiles.coverage_basis: A checked revision has complete conforming evidence, unavailable evidence, an incomplete inventory, or contradictory forbidden behavior.
semantic_profiles.exclusivity_basis: Completeness and availability are checked before behavior; any gap is inconclusive, any unavailable target is unknown, otherwise mutation/dependency evidence selects conforming or conflicting.
semantic_profiles.precedence: Inventory gap; unavailable target; forbidden behavior or divergence; complete conformance.
semantic_profiles.default_policy: Unknown or inconclusive evidence fails closed.

semantic_profiles.partial_data_behavior: Any missing/skipped surface makes the global claim inconclusive and failing.

invariants: Only generated exact-equality and typed outcome chokepoints decide compatibility.
Every public surface and shipped consumer is inventoried.
Advisory word scanning is never sufficient evidence.

failure_semantics.outcome: CI fails with the missing surface.

failure_semantics.class: Fake, SDK, or compatibility behavior divergence
failure_semantics.outcome: CI fails; fake is corrected rather than assertions weakened.

verification.method: Closed inventory, dependency ownership lint, projection drift, shared scenarios, FakeVsReal, and compatibility mutation corpus.
verification.criterion: Every gap and each range/dual-decode/degradation/renamed-retry/unregistered-surface mutation fails.

witnesses.precondition: Inventory covers every declared surface at one revision.
witnesses.stimulus: Run compatibility profile, SDK generation, simulator/fake, and scenario matrix.
expected_observables: All registered exact-match paths pass and evidence is complete.
forbidden_outcomes: Skipped target or unverified global claim.

witnesses.precondition: A target is unavailable or a mutation adds an unregistered route/host/decoder/retry site or compatibility behavior under an unrelated name.
expected_observables: Inventory/dependency/scenario/mutation gate fails and names the unavailable target or violation class.
forbidden_outcomes: Passing because evidence was unavailable, a word scan missed the identifier, or a target was skipped.

resolved_issues.resolution: Adopted the suggested single 1-64 byte [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ header domain and constant-bounded exact comparison in FR-PROTO-001 and contract-version-and-evolution.
Adopted TokenAuth -> ProtocolVersionGate -> handler for protected routes and gate -> handler for explicit no-auth routes, with compound-input tests and no pre-auth version disclosure.
Moved the cross-host continuity contract to component-protocol-policy-enforcement and grounded every Web, Electron, and Windows hop in one scenario matrix.
Applied terminal mismatch semantics to Web, Workspace, and Windows through contract-client-continuity and shared operation/reconnect counters.
Added serverId/config-generation label snapshots and serverId/observation-generation mismatch evidence with replacement, removal, and stale-result behavior.
Replaced word-scan authority with a closed surface inventory, chokepoint ownership rules, scenario coverage, and mutation fixtures for renamed compatibility behavior.
Added the cross-language SDK ADR as a decision input and component authority; retained generated C#/Swift/Kotlin/TS and stdlib-only Go while forbidding legacy version authority/fallback.
